subject: Request: temporary quarterly invoicing / Net-90 due to procurement cadence
messages:
From: Dana Chen <dana.chen@cloudling.io>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudling.io>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary quarterly invoicing / Net-90 for initial deployment

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — the team is excited to move forward. Our procurement cycle is quarterly and they’re asking for consolidated invoices on a quarterly schedule for the first year while we align budgets across EU and US business units. Practically that means Cloudling would pay for three months of usage in a single invoice (Net-90) rather than monthly.

We understand this is non-standard. Our CFO (cc'ed) is prepared to sign a PO and provide a payment guarantee if it helps — we’re asking for a temporary pilot (Q3 only) and would revert to monthly after that. Can Redwood confirm whether this is something you can accommodate and if any concessions (billing holdback / security deposit / change in discount profile) would be required?

Attached: draft PO for Q3 (cloudling_po_draft.pdf).

Best,
Dana Chen
Head of Finance, Cloudling

---

From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Dana Chen <dana.chen@cloudling.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Procurement Team <procurement@cloudling.io>
Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary quarterly invoicing / Net-90 for initial deployment

Dana —

Appreciate the context and the draft PO. I looped in Karthik (deal desk / salesops) to run the impact and Marissa for exec sign-off because this is an exception to our standard billing cadence. Two quick clarifying items so we can model options:

- Do you need a hard Net-90 (invoice due 90 days) or a single quarterly invoice with Net-30 from invoice date? The PO language appears to request Net-90.
- Is the PO covering committed spend (reserved capacity) or is this purely consumption-based for Q3? If committed, we can explore different protections.

We can propose a middle path: accept a single quarterly invoice but require a security deposit equal to one month of estimated spend (to mitigate receivable risk) and keep pricing as-is (no additional discount). If Cloudling needs a lower up-front cash burden, we can discuss a one-time reduced discount in exchange for the Net-90 term. Karthik, can you run the impact with those two scenarios and attach the short calc?

I'll wait for your reply and escalate to Marissa once we have the numbers.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai

---

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, Dana Chen <dana.chen@cloudling.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary quarterly invoicing / Net-90 for initial deployment

Avery / Dana —

Attached is a short impact spreadsheet (payment_impact_calc.xlsx) and a one-page terms summary (redwood_terms_summary.pdf). Quick callouts from ops & finance:

- Scenario A (Quarterly invoice, Net-30 from invoice date): 0% change to price; AR exposure window up to ~75 days depending on invoice date. Suggested contract language: invoice issued on last business day of quarter, payment due 30 days thereafter.
- Scenario B (Net-90): increases our effective DSO and requires mitigation. Finance recommends either (1) a security deposit equal to 1x estimated monthly invoice OR (2) a temporary reduction in the established discount from 12% -> 8% for Q3 only.
- For either scenario we should limit pilot to Q3 with automatic reversion to standard monthly billing unless both parties agree in writing to extend.
- There is an additional compliance consideration: Cloudling indicated they have EU data residency constraints. From a billing perspective that doesn't change the payment term, but we should confirm whether invoicing needs to be routed to EU finance (VAT and tax impact).

Impact numbers: with Cloudling's estimated Q3 consumption (~$210k/month), Net-90 would increase working capital exposure by ~$420k (two months) vs monthly billing. The deposit covers ~33% of that exposure. Discount trade lowers margin by ~$25k over the quarter vs deposit approach.

Recommend: Marissa — approval to accept Scenario B only if Cloudling provides either security deposit or accepts reduced discount for Q3, and on condition that legal signs off on PO language and tax routing. If you prefer, we can accept Scenario A without executive approval.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Deal Desk Manager | Redwood Inference

---

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Dana Chen <dana.chen@cloudling.io>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary quarterly invoicing / Net-90 for initial deployment

Thanks for the clear options and numbers. I reviewed the attachment and talked briefly with Finance. Approve the temporary Net-90 pilot under these explicit conditions:

1) Cloudling signs the PO as submitted and provides a security deposit equal to one month of estimated usage (wire prior to first invoice).
2) The pilot term is Q3 2027 only — we will revert to monthly billing starting 2027-10-01 unless both parties execute an amendment.
3) Legal to confirm PO language includes: (a) Redwood right to apply deposit to outstanding invoices after 60 days past due, (b) interest on late payments at Redwood standard policy, (c) tax routing confirmation for EU invoicing if needed.
4) No change to list pricing for the term (no additional discount); if Cloudling requests a discount instead of deposit we will decline unless there is a multi-quarter committed spend amendment.

Avery — please capture these terms in an amendment and share DocuSign link for Cloudling signature. Karthik — please note for AR and billing setup; Finance will expect the deposit wire reference before first invoice. Dana — once the deposit clears, we will switch your billing cadence for Q3 and issue the consolidated invoice at quarter close.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
